fluff.overview: The Mad Cat Mk II is a ninety-ton Clan assault BattleMech developed by Clan Diamond Shark beginning in the early 3060s. Designed explicitly as a commercial venture to bolster Diamond Shark profits following the costly Clan Invasion of the Inner Sphere, the design drew heavily upon the legendary Timber Wolf OmniMech as its foundation. Diamond Shark engineers based the new chassis on an existing BattleMech design to dramatically reduce development time, bringing the Mad Cat Mk II from concept to full-scale production in less than fifteen months. Unlike its OmniMech predecessor, the Mad Cat Mk II is a standard BattleMech, purpose-built for export to other Clans and, eventually, Inner Sphere buyers. The deliberate use of the Inner Sphere reporting name "Mad Cat" rather than "Timber Wolf" signaled Diamond Shark willingness to market directly to non-Clan customers, representing a significant shift in Clan mercantile philosophy.
fluff.capabilities:
Though bearing a remarkable outward resemblance to the Timber Wolf, the Mad Cat Mk II is an entirely new and powerful creation. Thirteen tons of ferro-fibrous armor mounted on a DSAM Endo 4 chassis provide exceptional protection for an assault-class design, while a Type 79 360-rated XL fusion engine drives the ninety-ton frame to a fast 64 kph. Grandthrust Mk. 5 jump jets grant the 'Mech a ninety-meter jump capability, making it remarkably agile for its weight class and able to traverse all but the most impassable terrain.

The primary armament consists of a pair of arm-mounted EMRG "Galaxy" Series Gauss rifles supported by torso-mounted Type X "Short Bow" LRM-10 launchers, giving the Mad Cat Mk II devastating firepower at range and indirect fire capability. Four Series 2b extended-range medium lasers in the torsos provide effective close-range defense. While the design can engage targets at extreme distances, it performs best within 450 meters where all weapons can be brought to bear simultaneously, delivering a steady volume of fire without risking redlining or reactor shutdown. Interestingly, the Diamond Shark technicians equipped the chassis with weapons drawn from their oldest Brian Caches, necessitating structural adjustments such as additional venting ports above the Gauss rifle mounts.
fluff.history:
The Mad Cat Mk II entered production in 3061 at Manufacturing Plant DSF-94 on Vinton in the Clan Homeworlds. Clan Diamond Shark conceived the design purely as a profit-generating venture after the Clan Invasion of the 3050s left even the home Clans reeling from the consequences of war. Taking inspiration from their successful Ha Otoko line, Diamond Shark leadership directed engineers to create a standard BattleMech that could be sold to fellow Clans seeking to rebuild their toumans.

Despite the design's considerable capabilities, its most obvious potential customers proved reluctant buyers. Clan Wolf and Clan Jade Falcon (once the strongest and most feared of the invading Clans) purchased none, though both acquired examples through Trials of Possession. Clan Ice Hellion and Clan Steel Viper also obtained small numbers through similar means. Only Clan Nova Cat purchased the Mad Cat Mk II in significant quantities, fielding them in considerable numbers during the tumultuous years surrounding the Jihad.

Diamond Shark sales strategy proved more successful with Inner Sphere customers. On a limited basis, unmodified Mad Cat Mk IIs were sold to the Draconis Combine and the former Federated Commonwealth states, with the Lyran Alliance also purchasing an unknown number. The decision to use the Inner Sphere "Mad Cat" designation rather than the Clan "Timber Wolf" name lent credence to the theory that Diamond Shark was willing to sell unmodified Clan equipment to the Inner Sphere, representing a significant shift in Clan attitudes toward commerce with the successor states.

During the Jihad, production at the Vinton facility ceased and the line was relocated to Manufacturing Plant DSF-IT1 on Itabaiana around 3071, where Clan Diamond Shark (later renamed Clan Sea Fox) continued to expand the line. The Mad Cat Mk II Enhanced entered production in the mid-3080s as a modernized variant designed to recapture declining sales, and proved to be one of Diamond Shark's bestselling products, competing only with the new Mad Cat III for commercial dominance. Subsequent variants including the "Super Mad Cat" and other specialized configurations were initially proprietary before being released to the open market, ensuring the Mad Cat Mk II family remained a cornerstone of Clan Sea Fox's commercial military offerings well into the thirty-second century.
fluff.deployment: A significant departure from the original design philosophy, this variant removes the Gauss rifles and jump jets entirely, replacing them with a pair of arm-mounted Hyper-Assault Gauss 30 cannons that deliver devastating suppressive fire. Each side torso retains an LRM-10 launcher and mounts a pair of extended-range medium lasers, while a Light Active Probe in the head provides enhanced sensor coverage for detecting hidden units. The tonnage saved by eliminating the jump jets and one heat sink is dedicated to additional armor protection, making this variant a heavily armored fire-support platform optimized for sustained engagements where raw battlefield presence outweighs mobility.
